thesis: Cast an eight-mana Gishath off a dork-and-land ramp base, make one hit land, and let the reveal put Dinosaurs onto the battlefield in batches whose entry triggers pay in cards and bodies, until a committed trampling alpha ends it by commander damage.

stages.label: THE EIGHT-MANA CLIMB
stages.what_it_does: Pays for an eight-mana commander, then for the Dinosaurs he did not reveal. Three layers: every land but Kessig Wolf Run, plus Sol Ring and Arcane Signet; land search (Nature's Lore, Three Visits, Skyshroud Claim, Huatli's basic); and since v1.2.0 a crop of mana creatures (Bloom Tender, Faeburrow Elder, Drover of the Mighty, Ixalli's Lorekeeper, Intrepid Paleontologist, Atzocan Seer) above the big producers: Selvala (X equal to the greatest power you control), Mirari's Wake (one extra mana per land tapped), Regal Behemoth (one extra per land tapped, but only while you are the monarch, which combat damage to you takes away) and Hulking Raptor (a fixed {G}{G} each first main phase, which does not scale). Knight of the Stampede, Otepec Huntmaster and Urza's Incubator named Dinosaur discount every Dinosaur spell, Gishath included. Hunting Velociraptor's prowl {2}{R} applies only after a Dinosaur has dealt combat damage to a player this turn, so for Gishath it is a re-cast discount, not a first-cast one. Much of the colour is creature-only: Ixalli's Lorekeeper, Ancient Ziggurat, and Cavern, Secluded Courtyard and Unclaimed Territory named Dinosaur pay for Gishath but not for Overwhelming Stampede or Akroma's Will. deck-audit prices the declared ramp group (15 cards, not this whole stage) at 0.696 in the opening seven and drawn by turn six in 0.906 of games, mean turn 2.018.
cards: Huatli, Poet of Unity // Roar of the Fifth People

evidence.note: 16 of 48 here; the rest are in Mana II (14), Recursion (6), Bodies (5), Ramp (4) and Tutors (3)

stages.label: THE FIRST CONNECT
stages.what_it_does: Nothing in the deck is the engine until Gishath deals combat damage to a player: the trigger reveals that many cards and puts every Dinosaur among them onto the battlefield. Two things must resolve: the cast (eight mana, the stage above) and the hit. He has haste, vigilance and trample on his own card, so the connect needs size and a second count, not haste. Berserkers' Onslaught gives attackers double strike: two combat damage steps, two triggers (open_questions[2]); Akroma's Will's first mode and Boros Charm's third grant double strike for one turn, and they sit in protection because that is the mode they are usually held for. Sunfrill Imitator, attacking, can become a copy of Gishath and carry the same trigger, which the pilot's game 003 records happening (a log, not a stack). Kessig Wolf Run is a repeatable land pump: the reveal counts damage dealt, so every point that gets through is one more card. Gishath lives in the command zone, so he can never be revealed or tutored, and he is the stage's single point of failure; each removal costs commander tax rather than the card. The reveal is a PUT, not a cast: Zacama's 'if you cast it' untap does nothing through this door. No passing stack on this 99 resolves a connect (open_questions[0]).

evidence.note: Gishath and Sunfrill Imitator sit in Bodies, Berserkers' Onslaught in Ramp, Kessig Wolf Run in Mana II
wincon:combat; double strike by oracle text

stages.label: WHAT THE TOP OF THE LIBRARY HOLDS
stages.what_it_does: The reveal is only as good as the top of the library, and the 99 holds 28 Dinosaurs for it to find (Roaming Throne is a Golem in the library and does not count). Congregation at Dawn and Worldly Tutor put creatures on TOP at instant speed, and the stack has to be built ON the swing turn: cast earlier, your draw step takes the top card and Bonehoard Dracosaur's upkeep exiles two more, and Etali's attack trigger exiles one more, so the window is after those, in the declare-attackers or declare-blockers step before damage. Enlightened Tutor is a draw tutor, not a reveal tutor: its targets (Roaming Throne, Berserkers' Onslaught, Mirari's Wake, Garruk's Uprising) are not Dinosaur creature cards, so one left on top only spends a reveal slot and goes to the bottom; it is cast before your draw step. Natural Order eats a green mana creature for a green fatty straight onto the battlefield. Rishkar's Expertise draws off the greatest power on the board. Bonehoard Dracosaur exiles two off the top in each of your upkeeps for you to play; Etali exiles the top card of each library only when it attacks. Pugnacious Hammerskull is a cheap 6/6, power the payoffs count. There is no fodder stage: the creature sacrifices in the 99 are Natural Order's additional cost, Palani's Hatcher eating its own Eggs, and Atzocan Seer and Thrashing Brontodon sacrificing themselves. None is a theme.

evidence.note: 4 of 8 in Tutors; Bonehoard, Etali and Hammerskull in Bodies; Enlightened Tutor in Insurance

stages.label: WHAT AN ENTRY IS WORTH
stages.what_it_does: Turns each Dinosaur that arrives, revealed or cast, into cards, bodies or damage. Garruk's Uprising draws per entering creature of power 4 or greater and gives trample; Vaultborn Tyrant draws and gains 3 on the same condition; Earthshaker Dreadmaw draws one per other Dinosaur; Trumpeting Carnosaur discovers 5; Pantlaza discovers once a turn at the entering creature's toughness. Curious Altisaur draws per Dinosaur that deals combat damage to a player and Quartzwood Crasher makes an X/X token where X is all the combat damage your trampling creatures dealt that player (with Uprising's trample, the whole connect). Roaming Throne named Dinosaur makes a triggered ability of another Dinosaur you control trigger an additional time. Read off the oracle text that would cover Pantlaza, Vaultborn, Earthshaker, Wrathful Raptors and Gishath's own reveal, a second reveal off one hit; that last is the claim this model leans on most and no stack has resolved it (open_questions[1]). It never covers Garruk's Uprising, an enchantment. Wrathful Raptors converts damage dealt to your Dinosaurs into damage at a non-Dinosaur; deck-audit prices it alone at 0.071 in the opening seven, drawn by turn six in 0.172, and it is one of the brief's two single points of failure.

stages.label: WHAT THE BODIES POINT AT
stages.what_it_does: The removal suite, most of it riding on Dinosaurs so a reveal can deliver it free: Bronzebeak Foragers exiles a nonland permanent from each opponent, Itzquinth makes a Dinosaur fight-without-fighting, Thrashing Brontodon and Tranquil Frillback answer artifacts and enchantments (Frillback also exiles a graveyard). Swords to Plowshares and Path to Exile are the cheap instants. Blasphemous Act is the reset: thirteen to every creature, near-free on a full table. With Temple Altisaur out it is one-sided for your other Dinosaurs, which take 1 each; Altisaur protects only OTHER Dinosaurs, so it takes the full 13 itself, and with Wrathful Raptors every one of those amounts, Altisaur's 13 the largest, is dealt again to a non-Dinosaur target. That line was resolved by stack 004 on a board that also held Ripjaw Raptor, which v1.2.0 does not run, so under the non-basic rule it is not cited here (open_questions[3]). deck-audit prices the Act alone at 0.071 in the opening seven and the declared Act-plus-Altisaur pair drawn by turn six in 0.020 of games, mean turn 7.852.

evidence.note: 4 of 7 in Bodies; Swords and Path in Insurance; Blasphemous Act in Ramp

stages.label: KEEPING THE BOARD THROUGH THE ANSWER
stages.what_it_does: Tables wipe this deck, and the pilot's best games rebuilt faster than the table answered. Flawless Maneuver is free with a commander out; Heroic Intervention, Boros Charm's indestructible mode and Akroma's Will (both modes with a commander, including double strike and flying) cover destroy effects; Eerie Interlude blinks the board out of a wipe, and its end-step return is a simultaneous entry that fires every entry payoff in conversion. Temple Altisaur prevents all but 1 of any damage to your other Dinosaurs, a damage wipe included, but not to itself. Devil Dinosaur gives other Dinosaurs hexproof and +1/+1. Kinjalli's Sunwing makes opposing creatures enter tapped, so an opponent's haste creature cannot attack the turn it arrives (oracle text, no log: game 001's 'makes their creatures enter tapped' was played on V3, before Sunwing came in). deck-audit prices the declared five-card protection group at 0.312 in the opening seven and held by turn six in 0.526 of games.

evidence.note: the five spells are in Insurance; Devil Dinosaur, Temple Altisaur and Kinjalli's Sunwing in Ramp

stages.label: THE COMMITTED ALPHA
stages.what_it_does: Games end by commander damage or a wide trampling swing, and the pilot's log says both losses were a board that was ahead and attacks that were not committed. Overwhelming Stampede gives every creature you control trample and +X/+X, X the greatest power among them, Rydia's Return adds +3/+3 (or regrows two permanents), Regal Imperiosaur is a Dinosaur lord. Regisaur Alpha and Palani's Hatcher give other Dinosaurs haste, so the ones you CAST swing that turn; Gishath's reveal comes after attackers are declared, so revealed arrivals swing next turn. Ghalta and Mavren makes an attacking token as large as the greatest other attacker, Ghalta, Primal Hunger costs less per point of power, Carnage Tyrant is an uncounterable hexproof 7/6 trampler and Zacama a 9/9 trampler. Zacama's {2}{R} also pings a creature, one of four cards in the 99 that can damage your own Dinosaur for Wrathful Raptors, with Blasphemous Act, Itzquinth and Trumpeting Carnosaur's discard.

map_disagreements.why: The six mana creatures form their own city (city-5), and all six are ramp:dork and threat:body bodies; only Atzocan Seer carries 'recursion'. The label is a uniqueness fallback, not a reading: Bodies and Ramp, the city's two top families, were already taken by the larger cities 0 and 1, so it got the next unclaimed name (deck_map unique_names). The cost reducers sit with other 'Dinosaur spells you cast' text in Ramp, and the land-search sorceries with tutors on 'search your library'. What they share, paying for Gishath, is not in any one card's text.

Only four of its fourteen cards are mana (Hunting Velociraptor, Knight of the Stampede, Otepec Huntmaster, Urza's Incubator). The rest are protection (Devil Dinosaur, Temple Altisaur, Kinjalli's Sunwing), win conditions (Carnage Tyrant, Ghalta, Overwhelming Stampede, Regal Imperiosaur), Blasphemous Act, Berserkers' Onslaught and Roaming Throne. The city reads as statics about Dinosaurs or costs, and its label follows the four.
The engine starts on a combat event, a hit, and the cards that make it count twice or bigger are an enchantment, a land and a copy creature. No text is shared, so the map cannot see the stage at all.

The declared kit is about haste for the 7/6, but Gishath already has haste. Four of its seven members grant haste to OTHER Dinosaurs or reduce costs, so the group scatters because it mixes three jobs (proposed_goldfish_edits[0]).
Removal on a Dinosaur body clusters as a body, which is the point: a reveal can deliver Bronzebeak, Itzquinth, Brontodon or Frillback for free, where Swords and Path cannot be revealed.

map_disagreements.component: KEEPING THE BOARD THROUGH THE ANSWER
map_disagreements.why: The five protection spells agree with Insurance. The three permanents doing the same job on a body (Devil Dinosaur's hexproof, Temple Altisaur's prevention, Kinjalli's Sunwing's tapped entries) are statics and land in Ramp.
Pumps, lords, haste-granters and fat tramplers share a job (a lethal swing) but no text; Rydia's Return lands in Tutors on its regrowth mode.

findings.claim: Knight of the Stampede, Otepec Huntmaster and Urza's Incubator named Dinosaur discount every Dinosaur spell, Gishath included. Hunting Velociraptor's prowl {2}{R} applies only after a Dinosaur has dealt combat damage to a player this turn, so for Gishath it is a re-cast discount, not a first-cast one.
findings.note: Round-2 over-claim resolved. The three static reducers match their oracles: Knight '{2} less', Otepec '{1} less', Incubator '{2} less' for the chosen type. Velociraptor now has its own sentence, gated on prior combat damage, which matches its oracle ('if you dealt combat damage to a player this turn with a creature with any of its creature types'). Pedantic only: the gate is any creature sharing a type with the spell, so for Gishath an Avatar would also qualify, but the 99 has none, so 'a Dinosaur' is exact for this deck. Commander tax still stacks on the prowl cost, and 'discount' does not deny that. Length is 1391, under the cap. The audit figures in the stage (0.696 / 0.906 / 2.018) are unchanged from round 2, where they were re-derived. Mechanically checkable: flag a card whose oracle carries 'prowl' or 'if you dealt combat damage ... this turn' when it shares a sentence with 'cost(s) ... less' or 'discount' and no conditional word ('only', 'after', 'if').
